body.statement:
Let \(y=(y_0,\ldots,y_4)\in\mathbb R^5\), and define
\[
 M_2(y)=(y_{i+j})_{i,j=0}^2,
 \qquad M_1(xy)=(y_{i+j+1})_{i,j=0}^1.
\]
If \(M_2(y)\succ0\) and \(M_1(xy)\succ0\), then \(y\) has a finite
nonnegative representing measure on \([0,\infty)\).

source.locator: Theorem 3.2(ii), specialized to degree four and a positive-definite shifted block
source.verbatim_statement: Suppose S = 2m for some m in N. Then r is in M_S if and only if there exists zeta >= 0 such that H_m(r) is positive semidefinite and B_m^*(r,zeta) is positive semidefinite.
